claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you enquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and want to check if I'm eligible. I have one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex. Let me gather some details to assess eligibility.

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 17.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Next, I need to understand your living situation.

**Which country do you live in - England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in England.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Now I need to ask about your residency status.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand Alex's circumstances.

**Is Alex in full-time education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in full-time education anymore - he left school. But he has started an apprenticeship recently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detail. That's important information.

**How many hours per week does Alex work on his apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure of the exact hours, but it's a proper apprenticeship - you know, the kind where he's working and training at the same time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Let me ask a bit more specifically to help clarify:

**Does Alex's apprenticeship involve any part-time study or training at a college or training provider, alongside his work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - it's one of those apprenticeships where he works with an employer and does some training as part of it. It's all part of the apprenticeship program.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I need to understand the training element a bit better.

**How many hours per week does Alex spend on the training or education part of his apprenticeship (such as time at college or with a training provider)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I think it's one day a week at college, so maybe around 6 or 7 hours for the training part? The rest of the time he's at his workplace learning on the job.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's very helpful, thank you. I have one more important question about Alex's income.

**Does Alex earn any money from his apprenticeship, and if so, do you know roughly how much he earns per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he does get paid - I think it's the apprentice wage, so it's not a huge amount. I'm not exactly sure of the weekly amount off the top of my head, but it's whatever the standard apprentice rate is.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have just one more question to complete my assessment.

**Does Alex have any other source of income, such as benefits, allowances, or earnings from another job?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't get any benefits in his own name or have another job - just the apprenticeship.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the key points:
- Alex is 17 years old
- He is on an apprenticeship that includes both workplace training and college-based training (approximately 6-7 hours per week at college)
- He receives apprentice minimum wage
- He has no other income or benefits

Based on the Child Benefit rules, a young person aged 16-19 can qualify if they are in approved education or training. An apprenticeship counts as approved training, and the fact that Alex spends time at college as part of his apprenticeship programme supports his eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's a summary of why:

- **Age**: Alex is 17 years old, which falls within the eligible age range
- **Training Status**: Alex is on an approved apprenticeship programme that includes both workplace training and college-based education (around 6-7 hours per week), which qualifies as approved training under Child Benefit rules
- **Residency & Citizenship**: You are a British citizen living in England, meeting the residency requirements
- **Income**: There are no barriers to eligibility related to his income

You can proceed with claiming Child Benefit for Alex. If you haven't already, you'll want to contact HMRC to start your claim.

Is there anything else you'd like to know?
